title: Suspect in deadly Berlin Pride attack killed in confrontation with police, officials say
summary: A suspect in the vehicle attack near Berlin's Christopher Street Day Pride parade that killed one and injured 29 was shot dead by police after a nearly 24-hour manhunt. Authorities named him as Abdul Ballout and said prosecutors believe he had sought to join the Islamic State. Pride events were cancelled and investigations are ongoing.
content:
Published- July 26, 2026 11:20 pm IST - BERLIN

A candle burns beside flowers and mementos left at the Brandenburg Gate, after a deadly incident in which a vehicle crashed into a crowd near Berlin's annual Christopher Street Day Pride parade on July 25, 2026, leaving multiple people injured and the parade called off in Berlin, Germany.

The suspect in the deadly Berlin Pride attack that left one person dead and 29 injured was shot and killed by police during a confrontation on Sunday in a suburb of the city, authorities said.

Abdul Ballout, a German citizen with Lebanese roots, was killed following a search that lasted nearly 24 hours after the attack in downtown Berlin. Berlin prosecutors said the suspect had previously sought to join the militant Islamic State group.

A white van had driven into the Tiergarten park around 10 p.m., which is next to the route that the Pride march had passed along earlier, and hit several people before colliding with a tree.

Police could not say how many officers had been deployed to the scene but said it was \"definitely a lot of police.\"

Overall, more than 2,200 police officers have been on duty in Berlin since Saturday morning (July 25, 2026) to protect the Pride parade and other LGBTQ+ events in the city.

The Pride march was called off after the incident. Authorities said investigations are continuing into the motive and circumstances surrounding both the vehicle attack and the subsequent confrontation that led to the suspect's death. Local prosecutors and law enforcement agencies are coordinating inquiries and have not ruled out further developments as witnesses and forensic teams are interviewed.
